restrictions: Generic distinguished-point birthday collision search on the 64-byte two-block W[0..7]-prefix message family; no cryptanalytic weakness in 40-round SHA-256 is claimed and no full-width 256-bit collision is produced.
Full-width success probability (>= 0.390001) relies on H1-random-function-walk; exact machine/controller/recovery pricing relies on H2-machine-and-controller-accounting.

heuristics.statement: The iterated 256-bit Walk-B transition F(Y) = B(Y) XOR PD on the 64-byte two-block W[0..7]-prefix message family of 40-round SHA-256 behaves like a uniform random function on {0,1}^256 with respect to birthday collision hazard, distinguished-point hitting times (p = 2155 / 2^122), trail-length tails, and 47-bit key independence.
heuristics.scope: Complete 40-round SHA-256 (steps 0..39 on every padded block, standard FIPS 180-4 IV, padding, message schedule, and feed-forward) restricted to 64-byte messages with fixed 8-word prefix W[0..7] and affine offsets W[8+k] = Y_k - K[8+k] (k=2..7).
heuristics.extrapolation: Extrapolated from the van Oorschot-Wiener (1999) and Flajolet-Odlyzko (1990) random-function birthday theory together with two organizer-executed reduced-width experiments on the 64-byte W[0..7]-prefix 2-block digest map at w=16 (merging bounded DP walk, max_evals=265, dp_bits=2) and w=14 (fixed-budget M=127 collision rate near P=0.39), linked to Walk-B via deterministic 256/256 equivalence verification in selftest().
heuristics.limitations: Empirical reduced-width experiments at w=16 and w=14 on the 2-block digest map cannot prove the absence of structural correlations or non-random cycle behavior in F(Y) at full 256-bit width. If 40-round SHA-256 deviated significantly from a random function under F, the achieved success probability could fall below 0.39.

heuristics.statement: Under the collision-frontier-v5 256-bit word-RAM model (C(40) = 2896), each 256-bit ALU, branch, or memory operation costs 1 unit; the 43,548-gate zero-move body uses native 32-bit (4-byte) instructions (2-bit op + three 10-bit register indices for 863 <= 1,024 registers); the rolled 2-lane SIMD recovery program fits in 440 5-byte records executing at most 1,429 ops/step (1,249 verified arithmetic ops + 180 rolled loop/indexing/DP/checkpoint ops); the control/cascade/table routines fit in 1,250 5-byte records with 12-op/100-op Stage-2 filtering and 100,800 ops per DP table scan/insert/restart; and setup/emitter work is bounded by 600,000,000 operations within 1 MiB peak memory.
heuristics.scope: Applies to the full-width 256-bit word-RAM machine execution, memory accounting (1,047,826 B <= 2^20 B), and total-work ledger N = 57,746,901,490,653,995,611,753,326,179,604,236,486,070.
heuristics.extrapolation: The 43,548-gate body, 860-data-register Reverse-DAG zero-move allocation, 4-byte binary encoding, and 1,249-op 2-lane SIMD Walk-B arithmetic are explicitly constructed and verified bit-for-bit in experiments/sha256_r40_search.py; the static record envelopes for the rolled controller (1,250 records), recovery loop wrapper (440 records, +180 ops/step), and setup emitter (600,000,000 ops) are conservative accounting envelopes following published frontier conventions.
heuristics.limitations: No standalone compiled native assembly listing of the outer controller or rolled recovery loop is executed end-to-end on the host. If the controller or rolled recovery exceeded its declared static bytes or per-step overhead, table capacity or recovery work would shift slightly and require re-tuning (Tp, B).
